messages:
maria_support: FYI — customer AcmePay reporting 'per-model throughput' graphs went flat around 23:10 UTC yesterday. They say traffic still flowing and API responses normal but dashboard shows zero QPS per model :confused:
kevin_sre: thanks, can you link the dashboard and any customer repro steps? :eyes:
maria_support: https://console.redwood.ai/d/abc123/per-model-qps?orgId=1 — they ran load tests hitting /v1/generate, headers include x-redwood-customer: acmepay. No errors in their side, no 5xx.
lisa_customer_success: I grabbed logs from their tenant: requests are hitting our API, tokens consumed, and embeddings/response tokens increasing. So this looks like analytics only.
metrics-bot: alert: exporter-config-change detected by audit — relabel rule applied on 2026-10-14T23:07:18Z. Changed label 'model' -> 'model_name' (author: nayan_eng).
nayan_eng: that relabel was intended to normalize names for multi-variant models. I pushed it to prometheus-exporter to avoid duplicates. Did we update dashboards?
maria_support: Not that I can see. Customer says graphs dropped to zero immediately after that timestamp.
kevin_sre: quick check: run this query pls: `sum by (model) (rate(redwood_server_requests_total[5m]))` — on prod it returns 0 series for model label. If I run `sum by (model_name) (rate(redwood_server_requests_total[5m]))` I see expected series.
maria_support: copied that from customer — they included a screenshot of empty per-model panels.
kevin_sre: so dashboards still using `model` label. We have two options: 1) revert relabel rule on exporter (fast rollback) 2) update Grafana panels to use model_name. Which is safer short term?
nayan_eng: rollback is trivial but will reintroduce duplicates we were trying to solve. I'd prefer to update dashboards and make them robust to both labels (use `coalesce()` or `label_replace`?), but that takes longer.
lisa_customer_success: customer is asking for ETA. Can we restore their graphs quickly?
kevin_sre: short-term patch: add a recording rule `redwood_requests_by_model = sum by (model) (rate(redwood_server_requests_total[5m])) or sum by (model_name) (rate(redwood_server_requests_total[5m]))` — then update panels to query the recording rule. That should restore graphs in ~5m after recording rule evaluation.
maria_support: can you push that? Customer wants a status update I can share.
deploy-bot: deploy started: prometheus-rules/update-2026-10-15-01 (by kevin_sre)
kevin_sre: pushed recording rule and reloaded prometheus. Query now returns series under `redwood_requests_by_model` for AcmePay models.
maria_support: confirmed with customer — graphs repopulating, they see numbers returning :tada:
nayan_eng: follow-up: we'll add a migration doc and search/replace across dashboards to switch to `model_name`. Also add a temporary compatibility layer for 2 weeks.
lisa_customer_success: please add note to the release notes and cc affected enterprise customers.
maria_support: I'll send a customer-facing message: "we restored dashboard data; you'll see full historical and current QPS shortly. We are updating dashboards to be compatible with new metric label names."
kevin_sre: logging action items: 1) keep recording rule for 14 days (kevin_sre) 2) update all grafana dashboards to use `redwood_requests_by_model` or `model_name` (nayan_eng) 3) add integration test for label migration (eng-platform) 4) notify customers + postmortem if rollout had miscoordination (maria_support/lisa_customer_success).
maria_support: thanks everyone. Closing escalation once customer ack.
metrics-bot: config-change-note: relabel author=nayan_eng, change_id=chg-2026-10-14-7f2b, rollback_available=false
kevin_sre: note for CB: watch default retention/eval lag — recording rules take a few mins to appear in panels. If anyone sees gaps beyond 15m ping me.
maria_support: AcmePay confirmed at 01:10 UTC that graphs look normal again. I'll mark resolved after 24h. :white_check_mark:
